text: When a conv2d is already feasible at 123.5 MHz with par_rows=3 giving 1 px/cyc and its 8.1 ns critical path is a 24-bit adder carry chain, do not cut par_rows to 1, acc_width to 21, and tree_regs to 0 merely to save LUT: it raises Fmax to 167.8 MHz and cuts 40 LUTs but adds 3 DSPs and drops to 1/3 px/cyc, losing feasibility.

When the Gowin conv2d design is already feasible at 167.8 MHz with 3 DSPs and 249 LUTs, do not widen acc_width from 21 to 24 while adding tree_regs=1 and moving dsp_regs from out to in_pipe_out, because it shifts the critical path to out_data's 21-cell carry chain and drops Fmax to 116.6 MHz (-51.2 MHz) for only 6 LUTs saved; keep acc_width=21 and dsp_regs=out/tree_regs=0 unless a single-field isolation proves the LUT gain is worth the timing loss.

When a Gowin conv2d leaves its nine constant 8x8 multipliers in LUT fabric with dsp_regs='in_pipe_out' (dsp=0, LUT=297) while the carry-chain accumulator/tree sets the critical path, switch dsp_regs to 'out' to infer MULT18X18 multipliers, cutting 54 LUTs to 243 with only ~0.6 MHz fmax change because the carry-chain path is unchanged.

When a Gowin conv2d is limited by a carry-chain adder-tree stage (8.62 ns: 5.02 ns carry logic + 2.74 ns route) from a multiplier-output register to the tree register, adding one tree-register stage (tree_regs 1 to 2) only trims route to 2.50 ns, yielding +2.5 MHz (116.0 to 118.5 MHz) at +81 LUT and still infeasible—so attack the 5-ns carry logic via DSP inference or a narrower accumulator instead of spending registers on retiming.

When the Gowin conv2d is feasible at 118.5 MHz/378 LUT with a 24-bit fabric carry-chain accumulator and par_rows=3, do not cut par_rows to 1 and acc_width to 21 with dsp_regs out→in_pipe_out just to add 3 DSPs, because although it shortens the critical carry-chain logic from 5.08 to 3.67 ns, raises Fmax to 121.7 MHz (+3.2 MHz), and drops LUT to 238, it loses functional feasibility, so keep par_rows=3 and attack the carry chain with DSP multipliers/registered output instead.

Remove multiplier pipeline registers (dsp_regs=none) when par_rows=1 causes post-synthesis simulation X's on Gowin conv2d, switching to par_rows=3 so Yosys folds the nine constant-coefficient shift-adds into the adder tree; this fixes sim and drops 3 DSPs for +60 LUT and -1.4 MHz (Fmax 121.7→120.3 MHz), with the final adder-tree carry chain still critical (8.31 ns).

When Gowin conv2d par_rows=3 with dsp=0 is timing-limited by the final 24-bit adder-tree carry chain t2[0] (11 carry cells, ~7.5 ns of an 8.3 ns path), adding a multiplier-side pipeline stage (pipe_mul 1->2, in_pipe_out) leaves that path unchanged and drops Fmax by 4.4 MHz (120.3->115.9) for only 2 LUTs saved—so instead narrow acc_width to 21 or rebalance the adder tree.

When the Gowin conv2d's final adder-tree carry chain (t2[0], 5.02 ns logic + 2.75 ns route, 11 carry cells) pins fmax near 115.9 MHz, re-staging the multiplier to pipe_mul=[2,1] only cuts 10 LUTs and drops fmax to 114.7 MHz while leaving the carry chain unchanged, so target the accumulator/tree rather than multiplier pipelining.

When on Gowin conv2d the critical path is an 8.7 ns carry-chain adder tree (5.0 ns logic + 2.8 ns route) and LUTs (286) are the binding objective with fabric-mapped multipliers (dsp=0), do not add DSP registers on both input and output sides (dsp_regs=in_pipe_out+in_out): it raises LUTs to 304 (+18) and leaves fmax unchanged at 114.7 MHz, because the bottleneck is downstream in the carry chain, not at the multiplier.

On Gowin conv2d, when a 3-row parallel design is feasible at 114.7 MHz with the critical path being an 8.72 ns carry chain (5.02 ns logic + 2.84 ns route) from the multiplier register g_r[0].g_c[2].m to t2[0] and LUT count is the objective, do not remove the post-multiplier register (pipe_mul 1→0, dsp_regs in_out/in_pipe_out) because it yields zero Fmax/LUT/DSP change (304 LUT, 0 DSP, neutral), leaving that same carry chain as the bottleneck.

When a Gowin conv2d's 21-bit ~8-adder carry-chain tree from multiplier register to t2 is critical at 8.72 ns and already feasible at 114.7 MHz, avoid adding an extra register-only tree level (tree_regs 1->2), because it leaves the ~5.0 ns carry logic essentially unchanged, raises route from 2.84 ns to 3.46 ns for a 9.40 ns total, and drops Fmax to 106.4 MHz while costing +39 LUT and 0 DSP.

When a Gowin conv2d is already feasible at 121.7 MHz with 238 LUTs and the 8.22 ns critical path is the 15-cell out_data carry chain feeding acc, not the DSP multiplier interface, strip the constant-coefficient multiplier input-pipe register (pipe_mul 1->0) instead of retiming the accumulator, gaining 0.4 MHz and 1 LUT while DSP count stays 3 because the dead fabric register is removed and the accumulator carry chain remains critical.

When a Gowin conv2d is already feasible at 122.1 MHz with 237 LUTs and 3 DSPs and its critical path is a carry-chain accumulator, avoid raising par_rows from 1 to 3 and pipelining the multiplier, because it removes all 3 DSPs but adds 67 LUTs and changes fmax by only +0.1 MHz as the carry chain remains critical.

When a Gowin conv2d is timing-limited by the 8.18 ns carry-chain accumulator (t2[0]) at 122.2 MHz with 304 LUTs and 0 DSPs, collapse par_rows 3→1, tree_regs 1→0, and pipe_mul 1→0 to use 3 DSPs, gaining +36.2 MHz to 158.4 MHz and −52 LUTs to 252 by removing that carry chain from the critical path (new 6.31 ns).

On Gowin conv2d, when LUT count is the binding objective and there is ≥22% slack to the 100 MHz target, delete the 3x21 multiplier output registers (dsp_regs=none) to trade 36.1 MHz (158.4→122.3 MHz) for 16 LUTs (252→236) at constant 3 DSPs, since the merged multiply→20-cell output carry-chain path becomes the 8.18 ns critical path and only remains safe because 122.3 MHz still clears 100 MHz.

When Gowin conv2d is timing-limited by the 21-bit partial-sum carry chain at 122.3 MHz with DSP-combinational multipliers, add one adder-tree pipeline register (tree_regs 0→1) to move the critical path to line-buffer address logic, raising Fmax to 179.6 MHz (+57.3 MHz) at +21 LUT and no DSP change.

When a feasible Gowin conv2d has >50% timing slack (179.6 MHz vs 100 MHz) and is LUT-bound because the critical path sits in line-buffer/BRAM logic, add tree registers (0→2) and DSP-output pipeline registers (0→1) to cut LUTs 257→237 by eliminating accumulator-alignment muxes, accepting Fmax 122.1 MHz—still above the 100 MHz constraint.
